decisions.title: JCS input domain and hostile JSON rejection
decisions.issue: JCS requires I-JSON input but generic Go JSON decoding can accept or collapse representations that are unsafe for request identity.
interpretations: Let duplicate object names select a value
Require valid UTF-8, paired surrogates, unique names, and one complete JSON value
decisions.peer_behavior: The maintained canonicalize 4.0.0 peer and the production JCS implementation agree on accepted pinned RFC fixtures.
decisions.selected_behavior: JSON rejects malformed UTF-8, lone or malformed surrogates, duplicate names, trailing values, and numbers outside binary64 before returning canonical bytes.
decisions.rationale: Ambiguous input cannot safely identify a retried business request.
decisions.security_consequences: Duplicate-name and Unicode parser differentials fail closed.
decisions.resource_consequences: Validation occurs under explicit input and depth limits.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Inputs accepted by permissive JSON parsers can be rejected.
decisions.wire_consequences: Only one complete UTF-8 JSON value enters canonicalization.
decisions.reconsider_when: RFC 8785, its errata, or the accepted input policy changes.

decisions.title: JCS number serialization and negative zero policy
decisions.issue: RFC 8785 serializes binary64 values using ECMAScript rules and maps minus zero to zero, while request identity can treat a signed zero as suspicious input.
interpretations: Reject negative zero before JCS serialization
decisions.peer_behavior: canonicalize 4.0.0 serializes negative zero as 0 as required by RFC 8785.
decisions.selected_behavior: Finite binary64 numbers use RFC 8785 serialization, but negative zero is deliberately rejected as invalid payload.
decisions.rationale: Rejecting negative zero prevents a source-level distinction from silently collapsing in business identity.
decisions.resource_consequences: Number conversion is bounded to binary64.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: This defensive policy is stricter than RFC 8785 for negative zero.
decisions.wire_consequences: Accepted numbers emit ECMAScript-compatible shortest JSON spellings.
decisions.upstream_status: The negative-zero difference is deliberate package policy, not an RFC erratum.
decisions.reconsider_when: A new fingerprint policy version explicitly adopts RFC 8785 negative-zero equivalence.

decisions.title: JCS property ordering and Unicode preservation
decisions.issue: UTF-8 byte order, Unicode scalar order, locale order, and RFC-required UTF-16 code-unit order can differ for object property names.
interpretations: Sort raw property names by UTF-16 code units recursively
decisions.peer_behavior: The maintained canonicalize 4.0.0 peer agrees on the pinned RFC UTF-16 property-order fixture.
decisions.selected_behavior: Objects are recursively sorted by raw UTF-16 property-name code units, arrays retain element order, and output is UTF-8.
decisions.rationale: The RFC order is required for cross-runtime fingerprint agreement.
decisions.security_consequences: Locale and encoding-dependent property ordering cannot alter fingerprints.
decisions.resource_consequences: Sorting remains bounded by caller input, output, and depth limits.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: UTF-8-sorted encoders can produce incompatible fingerprints.
decisions.wire_consequences: Unicode strings are preserved without normalization while property order is deterministic.
decisions.upstream_status: No package-specific exception to RFC ordering is selected.
decisions.reconsider_when: A superseding canonical JSON profile changes ordering or Unicode treatment.

decisions.title: Canonicalization bounds and raw-byte policy
decisions.issue: RFC 8785 defines output bytes but does not define application resource limits or when already-canonical non-JSON bytes may be fingerprinted.
interpretations: Require explicit input, output, depth, and raw-byte limits
decisions.peer_behavior: General JCS peers do not own this package's hostile-input resource policy or non-JSON encoding contracts.
decisions.selected_behavior: JSON requires positive input, output, and depth limits; BytesFingerprint preserves exact bytes and requires a positive maximum.
decisions.rationale: Callers must choose the resource and encoding policy that defines business identity.
decisions.security_consequences: Untrusted canonicalization and hashing are bounded before authority is granted.
decisions.resource_consequences: Exact configured boundaries are accepted and the next byte or level is rejected.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Changing limits or raw encoding requires application review.
decisions.wire_consequences: BytesFingerprint performs no normalization or transcoding.
decisions.upstream_status: Resource and raw-byte policy are package-owned.
decisions.reconsider_when: A public profile defines different mandatory bounds or a non-JSON canonical encoding.

decisions.title: Fingerprint and correlation digest framing
decisions.issue: SHA-256 and HMAC define primitives but not fingerprint policy versions or collision-safe framing of logical key components.
interpretations: Hash canonical bytes without a policy version
Use SHA-256 fingerprints plus version comparison and length-framed HMAC-SHA-256 correlation
decisions.peer_behavior: Standard-library SHA-256 and HMAC implement the pinned RFC primitives; no external peer selects package framing.
decisions.selected_behavior: Fingerprints are a policy version plus SHA-256 of canonical bytes; diagnostic correlation is HMAC-SHA-256 over five length-prefixed key components.
decisions.rationale: Versions prevent silent canonicalization migration and length prefixes prevent concatenation ambiguity.
decisions.security_consequences: Correlation values do not expose raw logical keys and secrets require at least 32 bytes.
decisions.resource_consequences: Versions, key parts, and fixed-width digests are bounded.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: An identical digest under a different policy version is a conflict.
decisions.wire_consequences: Persisted fingerprint sums are exactly 32 bytes and correlation output is lowercase hexadecimal.
decisions.upstream_status: RFC 2104 supplies the HMAC construction as an additional authority.
decisions.reconsider_when: A versioned digest migration or correlation format is introduced.

decisions.title: JSON-RPC invocation projection and identity
decisions.issue: JSON-RPC defines full request objects but does not define which fields establish durable business idempotency identity.
interpretations: Project method and params while requiring an application-scoped key
decisions.peer_behavior: Full JSON-RPC servers bind transport IDs to responses but do not provide this package's durable business-key projection.
decisions.selected_behavior: Request projects only method and params; the application key operation must exactly equal method and the JSON-RPC id is not used as the business idempotency key.
decisions.rationale: Transport correlation IDs are not necessarily stable, unique business identities.
decisions.security_consequences: Tenant, caller, namespace, operation, and delivery identity remain explicit application inputs.
decisions.resource_consequences: Params fingerprinting is caller-owned and must be bounded.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Changing projected business fields requires a new fingerprint policy version.
decisions.wire_consequences: jsonrpc and id remain owned by the surrounding transport adapter.
decisions.upstream_status: JSON-RPC 2.0 has no separate errata feed; its publication index is monitored.
decisions.reconsider_when: A transport adapter standardizes durable key projection.

decisions.title: JSON-RPC result and error replay shape
decisions.issue: Durable replay must preserve the JSON-RPC result-or-error invariant without pretending to own the full response envelope.
interpretations: Store exactly one valid JSON result or one error object
decisions.peer_behavior: JSON-RPC 2.0 peers require result and error to be mutually exclusive.
decisions.selected_behavior: Response contains exactly one valid JSON result or an error with an integer code, nonempty message, and optional valid JSON data.
decisions.rationale: Replay must not manufacture a protocol-invalid semantic response.
decisions.security_consequences: Malformed persisted responses fail closed before handler execution.
decisions.resource_consequences: The versioned persisted response envelope is size-bounded.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Full jsonrpc and id members remain transport-owned and are not persisted here.
decisions.wire_consequences: Result and error JSON values are replayed through typed projection fields.
decisions.upstream_status: The projection follows the current JSON-RPC 2.0 result and error invariant.
decisions.reconsider_when: The adapter begins owning complete JSON-RPC response envelopes.

decisions.title: JSON-RPC error codes and internal failure mapping
decisions.issue: JSON-RPC reserves error ranges but leaves application errors open, and it does not define how an idempotency replay encoder failure should be represented.
interpretations: Rerun after invalid or oversized handler output
decisions.peer_behavior: JSON-RPC peers use -32603 for internal errors and permit application-defined codes outside reserved ranges.
decisions.selected_behavior: Caller error codes are preserved; invalid or oversized handler output is durably mapped to -32603 internal error and is not rerun.
decisions.rationale: A handler that already ran must not be silently repeated because its response cannot be replayed.
decisions.security_consequences: Invalid output becomes a bounded generic error without leaking payload details.
decisions.resource_consequences: The internal-error envelope fits the configured minimum response limit.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Applications own valid use of reserved and application error ranges.
decisions.wire_consequences: Terminal replay uses code -32603 and message internal error.
decisions.upstream_status: The -32603 mapping uses the current JSON-RPC predefined error.
decisions.reconsider_when: A versioned transport policy defines another terminal-error mapping.

decisions.title: JSON-RPC notification and batch ownership boundary
decisions.issue: JSON-RPC defines notification suppression and batch response assembly, while this middleware operates on one projected invocation without an id field.
interpretations: Require the transport to classify notifications and decompose batches
decisions.peer_behavior: Full JSON-RPC peers own request IDs, notification response suppression, batch scheduling, and response ordering.
decisions.selected_behavior: The middleware processes one invocation and does not classify notifications, assemble batches, emit ids, or choose batch ordering; the surrounding transport owns those rules.
decisions.rationale: The projection lacks the fields required to implement those protocol contracts correctly.
decisions.security_consequences: The middleware cannot accidentally emit a response to a notification on its own.
decisions.resource_consequences: Batch width and transport parsing remain outside this package.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Callers must not present idempotencyrpc as a complete JSON-RPC server.
decisions.wire_consequences: No full JSON-RPC request or response envelope is emitted.
decisions.upstream_status: Notification and batch rules remain normative at the transport boundary.
decisions.reconsider_when: A complete JSON-RPC transport adapter is added.

decisions.title: HTTP Idempotency-Key syntax and application scoping
decisions.issue: The draft defines an Item Structured Header string, while the package historically accepts one trimmed header value and delegates semantic validation and scoping.
interpretations: Require the application Key callback to construct a bounded five-part identity
decisions.peer_behavior: Draft-conforming HTTP peers serialize an sf-string; deployed provider profiles vary in accepted key syntax and scope.
decisions.selected_behavior: Middleware requires one nonempty trimmed Idempotency-Key value and delegates syntax plus namespace, tenant, operation, caller, and value scoping to Key.
decisions.rationale: The stable v1 API predates draft-07 syntax and application identity cannot be inferred from the header alone.
decisions.security_consequences: Applications must reject ambiguous or inappropriately scoped values in Key.
decisions.resource_consequences: Constructed key parts are bounded by the semantic core.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: The package does not claim full draft-07 structured-field conformance.
decisions.wire_consequences: Header quotes and structured-field escaping are not decoded by middleware.
decisions.upstream_status: The source is an expiring Internet-Draft and its Datatracker publication is monitored.
decisions.reconsider_when: The draft becomes an RFC or a new major version adopts structured-field parsing.

decisions.title: HTTP fingerprint conflicts and status mapping
decisions.issue: The draft recommends fingerprints and distinguishes concurrent 409 from different-payload 422, while the stable middleware exposes one conflict family.
interpretations: Expose package outcomes and let a higher transport profile remap them
decisions.peer_behavior: Draft-07 recommends 409 for concurrent work and 422 for key reuse with another payload.
decisions.selected_behavior: Missing or invalid identity returns 400, unavailable storage returns 503, and both in-progress and fingerprint conflict return 409 with distinct Idempotency-Outcome values.
decisions.rationale: Stable machine-readable outcomes preserve the distinction even though v1 shares one HTTP status.
decisions.security_consequences: Storage failure cannot authorize untracked handler execution.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: The 409 conflict mapping deliberately differs from draft-07's recommended 422 payload-conflict status.
decisions.wire_consequences: Every response carries Idempotency-Outcome and replay adds Idempotency-Replayed true.
decisions.upstream_status: Draft-07 status guidance is recommendation strength and remains work in progress.
decisions.reconsider_when: A major transport profile adopts distinct 409 and 422 mappings.

decisions.title: HTTP response replay and terminal failure policy
decisions.issue: HTTP and the Idempotency-Key draft do not define which response metadata is safe to persist or what to do after a handler produces an unreplayable response.
interpretations: Buffer a bounded status, selected headers, and body and persist terminal 500 on encoding failure
decisions.peer_behavior: Provider idempotency profiles differ on cached failures, header replay, retention, and response size.
decisions.selected_behavior: Middleware buffers one bounded response, persists only configured canonical header names, replays completed and terminal responses, and records terminal HTTP 500 after oversized output.
decisions.rationale: A handler that may have caused a side effect must not be rerun solely because replay encoding failed.
decisions.security_consequences: Secret, hop-by-hop, and unbounded headers are excluded unless callers explicitly misconfigure ReplayHeaders.
decisions.resource_consequences: Buffered and persisted response bytes have explicit maxima.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Streaming, flushing, hijacking, and full-duplex response interfaces are unsupported.
decisions.wire_consequences: Replayed status, selected headers, and body match the stored bounded projection.
decisions.upstream_status: This is a package transport profile constrained by RFC 9110, not an HTTP-wide requirement.
decisions.reconsider_when: A named external response-replay profile is adopted.

decisions.title: Durable enforcement, expiry, and fencing semantics
decisions.issue: The draft assigns key lifecycle and enforcement to the resource but does not define distributed ownership, crash ambiguity, takeover, or fencing.
interpretations: Treat a cache hit as exactly-once execution
Let process-local leases authorize distributed side effects
Use durable acquisition outcomes, bounded leases, monotonically increasing fences, and explicit unknown results
decisions.peer_behavior: HTTP idempotency implementations vary between caches, database uniqueness, durable state machines, and provider-specific replay stores.
decisions.selected_behavior: Durable stores elect one current owner, preserve completed or terminal replay, distinguish fingerprint conflict, and require application fencing because lease expiry never proves old work stopped.
decisions.rationale: Exactly-once execution cannot be inferred across process death and unrelated side-effect stores.
decisions.security_consequences: Unavailable durable ownership fails closed by default and stale owners cannot complete with old fences.
decisions.resource_consequences: Leases, results, metadata, keys, retention, and cleanup are bounded.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Process-local memory is not a multi-replica durability claim.
decisions.wire_consequences: Transport adapters project stable acquired, replayed, conflict, in-progress, terminal, and unavailable outcomes.
decisions.upstream_status: Distributed durability and fencing are package-owned additions to draft enforcement guidance.
decisions.reconsider_when: A standards profile defines equivalent crash, ownership, and fencing semantics.
